body:
```suggestion
		<signal name="state_started">
```
I made the same comment in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102165#pullrequestreview-2607672617. Avoid using the word "node".

It seems to me that the places to fire signals are scattered all over the place. Can you make a method to assign a state, for example, `fading_from = p_fading_from` and unify them there?

I think you can refer/salvage https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/88179/files#diff-9176faca3ecbebad6f340de9260278b31819bdfae318c1cd310a01c60229d0e7R196-R200, as I have requested same in there. Considering this PR, I think you can fire the `state_end` signal there if the argument is empty.

It is a not good way to connect signals every time you change the current. Also, it looks like the connection will remain even after changing to a state machine type other than Grouped.

There are two possible ways to do this correctly.

1. GroupedStateMachine directly calls the parent's Playback function without using a signal, as in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/88179/files#diff-9176faca3ecbebad6f340de9260278b31819bdfae318c1cd310a01c60229d0e7R202-R210.

2. Connect the signal. However, to avoid doing this too often, you should do it in `set_state_machine_type()` and `_tree_changed()` and disconnect the signals when it is not needed.

```suggestion
	void _clear_fading(AnimationNodeStateMachine *p_state_machine, const StringName p_state);
```

No need to be that much specific about the method name. Also, as I've said elsewhere, avoid ambiguous words like "maybe".

I ended up adding this logic to `_set_grouped` so it will connect/disconnect whenever the playback instance mode is changed. At first I preferred option 1 but the logic for `_get_parent_playback` seemed much more expensive vs `is_connected`. For option 2 I wasn't sure how to update all playback instances from the non-playback node outside of a process context, and even then I _think_ it would require a check in process anyways so checking if the value changes in `_set_grouped` seemed like the efficient approach. I still need to test that it handles if the state machine type changes at runtime but it handles the basic case at least.

As I commented above, this needs to be done on specific setters and on the changed signal of the animation tree, not in process.

There may not be much of a performance issue with doing the bool check in process each time.

Rather, it is a matter of consistency. As far as I know, there is no other class that implements bind in process that should be associated with a setter. In the extreme case, since they are not done immediately after the setter, any processing between the setter and process could cause problems if the states do not match.

The problem with using the setter + signals is that at no point besides process does the state machine or playback have reference to the tree, and so there's no parent playback to reference. I thought this change was appropriate as the playback's state and signals only change/emit during process (ie, it's already possible for the sm and playback to have mismatched states between process calls because the playback is always updated during process) and the original concern was characterized as `to avoid doing this too often` rather than process being entirely off limits. With that being the case, I'll change the code to avoid signals entirely and cache the parent playback.

I see, then it may be acceptable, but the following approach may be more preferable.

> GroupedStateMachine directly calls the parent's Playback function without using a signal, as in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/88179/files#diff-9176faca3ecbebad6f340de9260278b31819bdfae318c1cd310a01c60229d0e7R202-R210.

I'll finish up a version which bubbles up events from grouped SMs via method calls rather than signals for comparison. There's also a small benchmark I'd like to do for a related part of the code. Also while working on the non-signal version I realized this doesn't disconnect/reconnect on tree changes, so I'll change that as well.

The direct callback approach ended up being fairly clean. I experimented a bit with caching the tree + parent context on the playback instance but it was an extremely marginal improvement relative to the complexity that introduced.
